messages:
maria: Quick sync — packaging question. Pilot customer (fintech) wants predictability for 'interactive sessions' instead of purely per-token. Thinking a hybrid: session credits + token overlay. Need feedback on tradeoffs and launch criteria.

jordan: I like session credits for predictability. Question: how do we price idle vs active time?

lia: could treat idle keepalive as a tiny token drain (eg 1 token/min) so long idle sessions still incur minimal cost. but that makes the math noisy.

kevin: ops POV: or bill by concurrent-session-hours. E.g., $X / session-hour. Gives simple enforcement and matches capacity planning.

sylvia: also think about QoS lanes — some sessions need high-priority routing (low latency) vs best-effort. That changes SKU complexity if we tie sessions to lanes.

maria: Good point. Launch checklist should include pricing calc, billing integration (migration path), console UI for live concurrent sessions, and entitlements for Dedicated/Private. Also contract language for session caps.

jordan: Pilot ask specifics: 100 concurrent sessions + 10M tokens/month. They want a single committed monthly price with a cushion for sessions. Proposal: a "Session Pack" add-on that includes N concurrent sessions and a token bucket.

lia: I worry about mixing conversions (sessions -> tokens). Simpler: Session Pack covers concurrent capacity; overages after pack are billed per session-hour or per-token depending on whether session was active. We can offer a conversion discount but keep the default simple.

kevin: Technical enforcement: runtime must tag requests with session_id and session_type. Telemetry needs: session_id, last_active_ts, active_token_count, lane. Also an eviction policy for long-idle sessions. I'll raise an infra ticket.

sylvia: Compliance note: for Private customers we must expose session TTL and retention controls. Also audit logs for session lifecycle. Add to product requirements.

maria: Action items: PRD draft with SKU names and example invoices + SLO impact. @kevin to stub runtime telemetry schema. @lia to draft pricing model spreadsheet with examples. @sylvia to draft contract/entitlement blurb for session caps. Kickoff sync Friday 10am?

kevin: I'll create the infra ticket and initial telemetry schema: session_id, created_ts, last_active_ts, active_tokens, lane, tenant_id.

lia: I'll prototype a price calculator (session-hours vs tokens) and share before Friday.

sylvia: I'll pull relevant enterprise contract language and propose simple session-cap clauses + migration grace period.

maria: Also: avoid the word "burst" in customer docs here — call it "session cushion". Customers react badly to burst semantics.

deploy-bot: Reminder: any pricing SKU change requires a billing migration window and migration scripts. Please coordinate with billing eng.

maria: Thanks everyone — prep materials shared in #product-docs ahead of the Friday sync.
